column1: # Every tool option the live driver does not send, and the verdict on it.
# A live run is the only check that Drive agrees with this server, and
# until this file existed nobody knew what fraction of the tool surface
# one exercises. It reads 122 of 188 options. The shared standard names
# this gate for every repository with a live driver; the one other place
# it has been measured started at 14 of 28.
# Columns, tab-separated: tool.option, verdict, reason.
#   undrivable  no run from this account can send it, and the reason is
#               a second person, an administrator, or a state nothing
#               here may create.
#   undriven    a live step could send it and none does. The reason says
#               what it would take, because the point of measuring is to
#               close them, and a gap without a recipe gets read as a
#               decision.
# Fifty-two of these were closed in one sitting, which is the argument
# for recording a gap with its RECIPE rather than only its name: each row
# already said what would close it, so the work was a batch of small
# edits instead of a re-reading of the whole surface.
# `gates live-cover` holds both directions: an option that is neither
# driven nor listed here fails, and an option listed here that the driver
# has since started sending fails too. It runs in `make check` and CI
# against the binary's own published schema.
# What it CANNOT see is a step that exists and never runs — sitting in a
# slice nobody passes on, or behind a condition that was false. A sibling
# repository demonstrated that by deleting one call and watching its
# static gate still report full coverage. The driver prints its own
# recorded coverage at the end of every run for that reason, and names
# anything this file believes is driven that the run did not send.
copy_file.ocr_language
column3: it hints the language of text in a scan, for convert_to. Every fixture here is text somebody typed, and a copy of typed text has no OCR to hint

column1: delete_comment.reply
column3: deleting one reply needs the reply's id, which list_comments prints INDENTED under its thread rather than on an `id:` line — the shape mcpstdio.IDIn reads. Three of the four rows left here want the same missing piece: a reader for an id inside a listing

column1: download_file.acknowledge_abuse
column3: it needs a file Google has flagged as malware or spam, and nothing here may create one

column1: list_approvals.page_token
column3: a second page needs more approvals on one file than this run starts, and an edition allows one open approval at a time. This is the only one of the four that a reader for listed ids would not close

column1: list_labels.page_token
column3: no label is published to this account, so there is no first page to follow. The same blocker as the rest of the label surface

column1: manage_approval.replace_reviewers
column3: a swap names who takes the reviewer's place, so it needs a second address Drive will accept — the blocker spike F is waiting on

column1: reply_comment.reply
column3: editing a reply by its id needs that id, and the comments renderer prints it indented under the thread rather than on an `id:` line. Same missing piece as delete_comment.reply

column1: resolve_access_request.dry_run
column3: it needs a pending access request, which only somebody else asking for access can create

column1: resolve_access_request.notify
column3: the same pending request, and it would put mail in that person's inbox

column1: resolve_access_request.role
share_file.message
column3: it is only used when notify is true, which see

column1: share_file.notify
column3: it puts Google's mail in a real person's inbox on every run, which a driver may not do. The ownership transfer of spike F mails anyway, because Drive forces it

column1: unshare_file.permission_id
column3: list_permissions prints the id beside the grant rather than on an `id:` line, so the driver cannot lift it. Same missing piece again

column1: upload_file.ocr_language
column3: it needs a scan or a photograph to convert, and every fixture here is text somebody typed
